transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because... well, nothing really feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about things—checking out murals, going for runs, basketball, even just making a good drink at work. But lately, I just stand there. It's like I don't care about any of it.
Do you feel detached from yourself, as though you are observing yourself from outside your body?"

No, it's not like that. I don't feel like I'm floating outside my body or watching myself or anything. I'm still me, in my own head... I just feel empty. Like I'm going through the motions, but the part of me that used to care is just gone.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not seem to hear or see?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's really just... quiet in my head. Just empty.
Have you been feeling persistently sad or down lately?

I wouldn't really call it sad, no. I mean, I'm not sitting around crying or feeling down in the dumps. It's just... a whole lot of nothing. Like I said before, I just feel empty more than anything else. It's just a flatline.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about two months now. Yeah, right around two months. That's when the bar got bought out. Everything I had been working toward just... got changed. And since then, it's just been like this.
How much has this emptiness affected your ability to do your usual work and daily responsibilities?

It's affected things quite a bit, honestly. I mean, I've missed several shifts at work. And when I am there, I've been making closing mistakes that I never used to make. Now my coworkers have to double-check my work, which... well, people used to trust me to handle things. 

Outside of work, it's the same. I've stopped seeing my friends. We used to get together for runs, or to play basketball, or do these mural shoots, but... I just can't make myself show up anymore.
Since this began, have you noticed any significant change in your sleep?

Yeah, it's definitely changed. I'll lie down at night and I'm tired, but... my head just keeps going over every mistake I made at work. I just lay there thinking about it. And then when I finally do manage to get to sleep, I end up waking up around four or five in the morning, and I just can't get back down after that.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low in energy during the day?

Yeah, definitely. I just don't have the energy I usually do. Like at work, by the time I carry a couple cases of liquor from the back or just set up the well, my body feels like I've already worked a double shift. And that's even if I barely did anything that day. I'm just completely drained.
Since this began, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's actually been really frustrating. Doing inventory used to be completely automatic for me, I could do it in my sleep. But lately, I just stand there staring at the bottles, and I'll lose count like three times in a row. And even simple stuff, like... trying to decide which garnishes to restock for the shift. I just freeze up. I can't seem to figure it out.
Have you had any thoughts of being dead or hurting yourself?
No, I haven't really had any thoughts like that. I mean, I'm exhausted and frustrated with myself, but... I don't want to be dead or anything. I haven't thought about hurting myself.
Since this began, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Yeah, my appetite is pretty much gone. Most days I honestly just forget to eat. I won't even realize I haven't had anything until my hands start shaking while I'm working behind the bar. Then, maybe after closing, I'll try to grab a few bites of something cold, but... I just feel sick even looking at it. So, yeah, I'm definitely not eating like I used to.
Over the past two months, have you felt this emptiness or loss of interest nearly every day, for most of the day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. Most of the day, honestly. That's actually why I decided to come in, because... nothing really feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about things, you know? Going for runs, watching basketball, checking out local murals, even just making a really good drink for a customer. And now... I just stand there like I don't care about any of it.
